title: Titanium Connecting Rod
system: Engine Valve Train Components (Spring Retainers & Keepers)
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5, UNS R56400) was selected for this engine component application because its 900+ MPa tensile enables thin-wall lightweighting under cyclic loading. The alpha-beta microstructure provides 45% higher specific strength than 4140 steel, critical for weight-sensitive designs. Its 6.7 W/mK thermal conductivity simplifies thermal management. This rationale is driven by high-rpm engine connecting rod and specific design requirements.
process: CNC turn-mill multi-axis for engine component geometry
Shot peening Almen with 0.5mm corner radius
Black oxide/DLC coating with 0.5mm corner radius
CMM SPC dimensional check with 0.5mm corner radius
surfaceTreatment: DLC coating 2um, 15GPa hardness, 0.1mu friction coefficient applied to wear surfaces for extended durability — tailored for highrpm engine connecting application
commonFailures: Fatigue crack at thread-shank transition - prevented by larger fillet R0.5->1.5mm + cold rolling — critical for highrpm engine connecting performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Connecting Rod suitable for High-RPM engine connecting rod?
faq.a: Titanium Connecting Rod uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address engine component operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Connecting Rod?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Connecting Rod is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for highrpm engine connecting requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Connecting Rod require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. highrpm engine connecting components require DLC coating 2um, 15GPa hardness, 0.1mu friction coefficient applied to wear surfaces for extended durability — tailored for highrpm engine connecting application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Connecting Rod shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Connecting Rod includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet highrpm engine connecting specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for Con rod / Piston rod engine component components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
